answer: An island factory fires ivory pigment in kilns that share a monitored exhaust stack. The controller debits metered emissions against one stack budget and stops fuel feed at the cutoff. A hundred operator accounts still share that cutoff. More output within the budget needs cleaner firing. Inspectors must check that all exhaust crosses the meter, since a hidden vent evades the rule. Honest kilns lose production time if another kiln spends the budget.
